Home/Equations

Common heat transfer equations

Heat balance, exchanger sizing, tower performance, water balance, and pump and fan power, with a unit converter. U.S. customary units unless noted.

Jump to a section

01HVAC vs. Tower TonTwo different units 02Unit Converter13 conversion rows 03Heat BalanceWater, air, sensible & total 04Heat Exchanger SizingU, A, LMTD, effectiveness 05Cooling Tower PerformanceRange, approach, L/G 06Water BalanceEvaporation, cycles, makeup 07Flow, Pressure & PowerPump, fan, affinity laws

HVAC ton vs. cooling tower ton

HVAC & refrigeration ton

1 ton = 12,000 BTU/hr

Rates chillers, compressors, and HVAC equipment. Measured at the evaporator, the low-pressure side of the refrigeration cycle: refrigeration effect only. Written TR on this site.

≠

Nominal cooling tower ton

1 ton = 15,000 BTU/hr

Rates cooling towers. Measured at the condenser, the high-pressure side of the cycle, after the compressor adds its heat. Heat rejected by 3 GPM of condenser water cooled 10 °F. Written TT on this site.

Not interchangeable. The cooling tower serves the high-pressure (condenser) side, so it must reject the refrigeration load plus the compressor heat, roughly 15,000 BTU/hr for every 12,000 absorbed at the low-pressure (evaporator) side. For a typical chiller plant the two numbers are close, but they are different units. Confirm which one a spec sheet or quote uses. The Heat Load Calculator labels every result.

Unit converter

Enter a value on either side of a row.

Heat balance

Sensible heat — general form

Q = ṁ · cp · ΔT

Q = heat transfer rate (BTU/hr) · ṁ = mass flow rate (lb/hr) · cp = specific heat (BTU/lb·°F) · ΔT = temperature change (°F)

General form. The water and air equations below are this equation with density and specific heat combined into a constant.

Water-side heat load

Q = 500 · GPM · ΔT

Q = heat load (BTU/hr) · GPM = water flow (gal/min) · ΔT = temperature change (°F)

500 = 8.34 lb/gal × 60 min/hr × 1.0 BTU/lb·°F. Valid for water near ambient. 30% ethylene glycol is approximately 465; using 500 undersizes the flow.

Air-side heat load (sensible)

Q = 1.08 · CFM · ΔT

Q = sensible heat (BTU/hr) · CFM = air flow (ft³/min) · ΔT = dry bulb temperature change (°F)

Standard air at sea level (0.075 lb/ft³). Correct for altitude and high air temperature.

Total heat — air, including latent

Qtotal = 4.5 · CFM · Δh

Δh = enthalpy change (BTU/lb of dry air)

Use where moisture is added or removed, as in evaporative cooling. Sensible-only equations understate this load.

Heat exchanger sizing

Overall heat transfer rate

Q = U · A · LMTD · F

U = overall heat transfer coefficient (BTU/hr·ft²·°F) · A = surface area (ft²) · LMTD = log mean temperature difference (°F) · F = configuration correction factor (1.0 for true counterflow)

Solve for A to size an exchanger. Solve for U to check an installed unit for fouling.

Log mean temperature difference

LMTD = (ΔT₁ − ΔT₂) ÷ ln(ΔT₁ ÷ ΔT₂)

ΔT₁ = temperature difference at one end · ΔT₂ = temperature difference at the other end

For counterflow, ΔT₁ = Thot,in − Tcold,out and ΔT₂ = Thot,out − Tcold,in. If the two are nearly equal, use the arithmetic mean.

Overall coefficient from individual resistances

1/U = 1/hi + Rfi + x/k + Rfo + 1/ho

hi, ho = inside/outside film coefficients · Rfi, Rfo = fouling factors · x = wall thickness · k = wall thermal conductivity

Resistances in series. In industrial service the fouling terms usually dominate.

Effectiveness–NTU

ε = Qactual ÷ Qmax  |  NTU = U·A ÷ Cmin

ε = effectiveness (0–1) · Cmin = smaller of the two ṁ·cp products

Use when outlet temperatures are unknown. Qmax = Cmin · (Thot,in − Tcold,in).

Cooling tower performance

Range

Range = Thot water in − Tcold water out

Set by the heat load and circulating flow, not by the tower.

Approach

Approach = Tcold water out − Tambient wet bulb

Primary measure of tower capability. Wet bulb is the limit. Tower size and cost rise steeply below approximately 7 °F approach.

Tower efficiency

η = Range ÷ (Range + Approach) × 100%

Use to compare operating condition against design.

Liquid-to-gas ratio

L/G = ṁwater ÷ ṁair

Key parameter for fill and fan performance. Higher L/G requires more fill or airflow for the same approach.

Water balance

Evaporation rate

E ≈ 0.001 · GPM · Range

E = evaporation (GPM) · Range = cooling range (°F)

Approximately 1% of circulating flow per 10 °F of range. Varies with ambient conditions. Estimating only.

Cycles of concentration

COC = TDScirculating ÷ TDSmakeup

Conductivity or chloride ratios can also be used. Higher cycles reduce water and chemical use and reduce margin against scale and corrosion. Makeup water chemistry sets the limit.

Blowdown rate

B = E ÷ (COC − 1) − D

B = blowdown (GPM) · E = evaporation (GPM) · D = drift loss (GPM)

D (drift) is typically below 0.005% of circulating flow with modern eliminators. Higher on older or damaged eliminators.

Makeup water

M = E + B + D

Sum of all losses. Use to size makeup lines and estimate water cost.

Flow, pressure & power

Pump brake horsepower

BHP = (GPM · H · SG) ÷ (3960 · η)

H = total head (ft) · SG = specific gravity · η = pump efficiency (decimal)

3960 converts to horsepower for water. Divide by motor efficiency for electrical input power.

Fan brake horsepower

BHP = (CFM · SP) ÷ (6356 · η)

SP = static pressure (in. w.g.) · η = fan efficiency (decimal)

Fan power is a major share of tower and air cooled exchanger operating cost.

Affinity laws

Q₂/Q₁ = N₂/N₁  |  H₂/H₁ = (N₂/N₁)²  |  P₂/P₁ = (N₂/N₁)³

Q = flow · H = head/pressure · P = power · N = speed

Power varies with speed cubed. A 20% speed reduction cuts power approximately in half.

Reynolds number

Re = (ρ · V · D) ÷ μ

ρ = density · V = velocity · D = characteristic diameter · μ = dynamic viscosity

Laminar below approximately 2,300, turbulent above approximately 4,000. In turbulent flow, h varies roughly with Re0.8. Dropping into transitional or laminar flow reduces h sharply.

Reference only. Site conditions, fluid properties, fouling allowances, and code requirements apply to any specific application.

Notes on the calculations

Fluid properties

Specific gravity, specific heat, and freeze point interpolated from published glycol data at typical loop temperatures. Design-point values.

Evaporative vs. dry

Evaporative equipment is limited by wet bulb, dry equipment by dry bulb. Results outside these limits are rejected.

Exchanger sizing

Duty from the hot-side heat balance. Counterflow LMTD, with TEMA F correction for 1-2 shell and tube.

Home/Services/Inspections & Assessments

Inspections and assessments

Condition inspections and thermal performance assessments for cooling towers, fluid coolers, air cooled heat exchangers, and heat exchangers.

Condition inspection

Cooling towers:

  • Structure and casing
  • Fill and drift eliminators
  • Hot water distribution and nozzles
  • Cold water basin and louvers
  • Fans, drive shafts, gear reducers, and motors (visual)

Fluid coolers and exchangers:

  • Spray system and nozzles
  • Coil or tube bundle condition
  • Gaskets
  • Fouling and corrosion

Performance assessment

Field measurement of water flow, hot and cold water temperatures, and wet bulb. Range, approach, and heat load are calculated and compared with design conditions to show the capacity shortfall and its likely cause.

Home/Services/Tower Component Replacement

Cooling tower component replacement

Replacement of worn or damaged components on crossflow and counterflow towers, factory-assembled and field-erected.

Effect on performance

  • Fouled or collapsed fill reduces air-water contact and raises cold water temperature.
  • Damaged drift eliminators increase drift loss, water use, and chemical use.
  • Plugged nozzles leave dry areas in the fill.

Component replacement restores design performance at a fraction of the cost of a new tower.

Components

Fill

Film and splash fill, counterflow and crossflow.

Drift eliminators

Cellular and blade type.

Water distribution

Nozzles, branch arms, headers, hot water basins and covers.

Louvers

Air inlet louvers.

Casing and access

Casing panels, access doors, ladders, handrails.

Basin and structure

Cold water basin components. Structural members in wood, FRP, and steel.

Privacy policy

Last updated: October 26, 2026

TODO — fill in the legal entity name (e.g. “Heat Transfer Technologies, LLC”), state of organization, mailing address, and privacy contact email, then have counsel review this page before launch.

Scope

This policy covers information collected through this website by Heat Transfer Technologies (“we”, “us”). It does not cover information collected offline or through other websites.

Information we collect

  • Information you submit. Name, company, email, phone, state, and the details of your request when you use the request form or contact us.
  • Technical data. Our hosting provider records standard server logs (IP address, browser type, pages requested, date and time) for security and operation of the site.
  • Calculator and lookup inputs. Values entered in the heat load calculator and ZIP code lookup are processed in your browser and are not sent to us.

Cookies and tracking

This site does not set cookies and does not use analytics, advertising, or tracking tools. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, which receives your IP address when the page loads. See Google’s privacy policy for how Google handles that data. Because we do not track visitors across sites, we do not respond differently to browser “Do Not Track” signals.

How we use information

  • To respond to requests for parts, service, and information.
  • To prepare quotes and perform work you request.
  • To operate, secure, and improve the website.
  • To comply with legal obligations.

Sharing

We do not sell or rent personal information. We share it only with service providers that host the website or process form submissions for us, with suppliers where needed to fulfill your request, or where required by law.

Retention

We keep request information as long as needed to respond, maintain business records, and meet legal requirements.

Security

The site is served over HTTPS. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

Your choices

You may ask us to access, correct, or delete personal information you have submitted. Contact us using the details below. Residents of some states have additional rights under state law; we will respond to requests as required by applicable law.

Children

This site is intended for business users. We do not knowingly collect information from children under 13.

Changes

We may update this policy. Changes take effect when posted on this page, with a new “Last updated” date.

Contact

Privacy questions: see the Find Your Representative page for contact information.
